summary: Apollo config-center snapshot (1.8.0-SNAPSHOT, 819 readable source/config files; test sources are not present in the assigned scope). I traced the portal's authentication/authorization boundary end to end: Spring Security config (AuthConfiguration), method-level @PreAuthorize usage across portal and openapi controllers, the OpenAPI token filter, the access-key filter in the config service, and the role/permission services. The single strongest issue found is a missing authorization check on the portal endpoint GET /consumers/by-appId, which returns the OpenAPI consumer token (a credential validated by ConsumerAuthenticationFilter) for any caller-supplied appId. Every other sensitive portal endpoint in the same controller is guarded by @PreAuthorize("@permissionValidator.isSuperAdmin()"), and the portal UI that displays the token is gated on isRootUser, which indicates the endpoint is intended to be restricted. I did not find evidence of command execution, SQL injection, deserialization, XXE, or path traversal sinks in the reviewed code; the note/listener resolution, YAML parsing (SafeConstructor), and JDBC access are parameterized or type-limited.

Static, source-only review of the assigned xwiki-commons snapshot (parent POM version 13.8-SNAPSHOT; 1391 model-visible files, main sources/resource/POMs only, test sources not present in the snapshot). I inspected the security-relevant areas first (xml/HTML cleaning, filter streams, extension manager and repositories, job status/logging, XStream, velocity sandbox, crypto, classloader, websocket, diff) and traced input-to-sink paths. The single strongest candidate is an XML External Entity (XXE) flaw in the extension-descriptor parser DefaultExtensionSerializer, whose DOM parser is created with JDK defaults and no entity hardening while parsing descriptors that originate from remote extension repositories and installed/scanned extension artifacts. Several other plausible leads (StAX/Woodstox XXE in the XML filter path, non-restricted HTML cleaning in the HTML diff, job-status path handling, XStream without type whitelist) are recorded as unconfirmed rejected leads. No code was executed and no runtime confirmation is claimed.

Reviewed the LemMinX 0.18.5-SNAPSHOT XML language-server source (442 files; main sources, docs, build; no tests, no dependency jars). One candidate is submitted: external entity resolution is left enabled in the DTD/XML-Schema grammar-parsing paths, so the project's XXE mitigation (setting `xml.validation.resolveExternalEntities`, default false, plus a Xerces entity-expansion SecurityManager in LSPXMLParserConfiguration) is silently bypassed for attacker-controlled `.xsd`/`.dtd` content. Opening or editing a crafted XSD/DTD document makes the server parse it through Xerces loaders that resolve SYSTEM entities via the LSP URI resolver (local files and remote URLs), with no entity-expansion limit. This is offered as a lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability. Other suspicious areas (cache path handling, download-by-design behavior, resolver bookkeeping) are recorded as rejected leads.

Reviewed the Vaadin Flow (flow-project 2.6-SNAPSHOT) snapshot, concentrating on flow-server request handling: bootstrap/web-component bootstrap, UIDL/RPC handling, CSRF/push-id checks, stream resources/receivers, static file serving, path-safety helpers, dev-mode proxy and frontend installer. The single strongest source-supported lead is a reflected/DOM cross-site scripting path in the web-component bootstrap handler: the request-controlled `url` parameter is used verbatim as the application's service URL and is then serialized into the inline bootstrap `config` JSON without HTML escaping, while the sibling `initialUIDL` JSON is explicitly `<`-escaped at the same call site. Several other suspicious spots (zip-slip in the Node archive extractor, request-URI based redirect in VaadinServlet, Accept-Encoding q-value parsing, header copy in the dev-mode proxy) were checked and rejected or kept as unconfirmed leads because attacker control or impact is materially weaker or requires unusual preconditions.
